title: Clifford Cocks
name: Clifford Cocks
summary: British mathematician whose classified GCHQ work in 1973 developed a practical public-key encryption method later recognised as closely related to RSA.
whyThisMatters: Cocks’s work illustrates an essential distinction in security history: a result can be independently discovered under classification without shaping the public research community until it is disclosed.

sections.overview:
Clifford Cocks is a British mathematician and cryptographer. After research in number theory at Oxford, he joined the UK government cryptographic service in 1973.

Public-key work under classification

Responding to the challenge posed by James Ellis’s non-secret-encryption idea, Cocks developed a practical public-key encryption method in 1973. The work remained classified and was disclosed only in 1997; it therefore did not influence RSA’s independent public development.

Later recognition

The Royal Society credits Cocks with a 1973 practical public-key method and a 1998 identity-based-encryption discovery. He is included here for that carefully documented technical history rather than for a claim of sole priority.

timeline.event: Graduates from King’s College, Cambridge, and researches number theory at Oxford.
Joins the UK government cryptographic service and develops a practical public-key method.
GCHQ publicly discloses the earlier work.
Elected Fellow of the Royal Society.
